The trials are initially taking place at Amazon's robotics research and development facility near Seattle. The primary task for Digit in these early stages is to assist with tote recycling, a repetitive job that involves picking up and moving empty totes. This move is an expansion of the partnership between the two companies, as Agility Robotics is part of the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund. The Digit robot is designed to work in spaces intended for humans, and Amazon sees this as an opportunity to scale mobile manipulator solutions that can collaborate with employees. While the trials are a major development, Amazon has indicated that the robot is still in a testing phase to determine its helpfulness and is not yet deployed in regular operations. Agility Robotics plans to make the first Digit robots available to its partners in 2024, with broader market availability expected in 2025. <2> At its annual 'Delivering the Future' event on October 18, 2023, Amazon announced several advancements in its fulfillment center robotics. The main reveal was a new system named Sequoia, which integrates mobile robots, gantry systems, and robotic arms. [2] Amazon claims Sequoia can identify and store inventory up to 75% faster and reduce order processing time by up to 25%. [2, 6, 8] This system is already operational in a Houston, Texas, fulfillment center. [2, 6] The company also highlighted the roles of its existing robotic systems, including Proteus, its first autonomous mobile robot, and Sparrow, a robotic arm for handling individual items. [2] In addition to Sequoia, Amazon announced it would begin testing Digit, a bipedal robot, for repetitive tasks like tote recycling. [8] <3> Amazon confirmed it began testing the bipedal robot 'Digit,' developed by Agility Robotics, at a research and development facility south of Seattle as part of a broader investment in automation. [1, 2] The robot, which stands 5 feet 9 inches tall and weighs 143 pounds, is designed to work collaboratively with human employees in spaces built for people. [1, 4] Its initial task in the test phase involves tote recycling, a repetitive process of moving empty containers after inventory has been removed from them. [1, 2] Amazon has stated the goal is to have Digit handle repetitive tasks, freeing up employees for other work and supporting workplace safety, not to replace human workers who they deem 'irreplaceable'. [1, 4] This initiative was announced at Amazon's 'Delivering the Future' event and is part of the company's ongoing integration of over 750,000 robotic systems to work alongside its employees. [1, 10] <4> The U.S. Army conducted a Soldier Experimentation event with Robotic Combat Vehicle (Light), or RCV(L), prototypes at the National Training Center in Fort Irwin, California. [3] This experimentation occurred between July and September 2023 and was designed to assess the integration of these robotic platforms into Army formations. [3] The insights and soldier feedback gathered from these exercises are intended to inform the requirements and acquisition strategies for the RCV program of record, which is a key part of the Army's modernization efforts. [7] <5> In an article published on October 16, 2023, Nasdaq highlighted the increasing corporate appeal of robotics and automation as a response to rising employee wages and labor force instability. The analysis identified key growth trends for 2024, including the application of robotics in factory and warehouse logistics, the use of kiosk ordering systems, and the implementation of AI-powered software solutions. <6> Rockwell Automation, a global leader in industrial automation and digital transformation, has finalized its acquisition of Clearpath Robotics Inc., including its industrial division, OTTO Motors. The official announcement on October 2, 2023, confirmed the completion of the deal, which integrates Clearpath's expertise in autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and navigation software with Rockwell's extensive automation portfolio. This strategic move is poised to create end-to-end autonomous production logistics solutions, addressing complex and inefficient material handling tasks within manufacturing facilities. The acquisition, which includes both the Clearpath research division and OTTO Motors, will see both entities report to Rockwell's Intelligent Devices operating segment. The deal is valued at approximately $565 million in cash, with potential for an additional $50 million in contingent consideration. This combination aims to enhance productivity and safety, transforming the workflow throughout manufacturing plants and bringing the vision of the Connected Enterprise to life. <7> On September 19, 2023, the Toyota Research Institute (TRI) announced a significant advancement in robotics, unveiling a new generative AI approach called Diffusion Policy. This method allows robots to learn new, complex, and dexterous skills quickly from a small number of human demonstrations, eliminating the need for new code for each skill. This development is considered a key step toward creating "Large Behavior Models" (LBMs) for robotics, which are analogous to the Large Language Models (LLMs) that have transformed conversational AI. Using this single, unified method, TRI has successfully taught its robots over 60 varied skills, such as pouring liquids, using tools, and handling deformable objects like cloth. At the time of the announcement, TRI stated it was on pace to teach the robots hundreds of new skills by the end of 2023, with a further goal of reaching over 1,000 skills by the end of 2024. <8> On September 18, 2023, Agility Robotics announced its plan to open RoboFab, the world's first factory for mass-producing commercial humanoid robots, in Salem, Oregon. [1, 2] The 70,000-square-foot facility is designed to manufacture the company's bipedal Digit robot, with a projected capacity of over 10,000 units annually. [1, 3, 4] Construction on the factory began in 2022, and it was expected to open later in 2023. [1, 2] The company anticipates producing hundreds of Digit robots in the first year of operation, with the first deliveries for customers in the Agility Partner Program (APP) scheduled for 2024 and general market availability in 2025. [1, 5, 6] At full capacity, RoboFab is expected to employ over 500 workers, and Digit robots will also work in the factory performing logistics tasks like moving materials. [2, 6, 8] <9> Researchers at Cornell University have developed an insect-sized, 3D-printed quadruped robot powered by the combustion of methane and oxygen, a departure from typical electrically-powered micro-robots. [2, 5] This innovation stems from the Organic Robotics Lab, led by associate professor Rob Shepherd. [2] The research, detailed in the paper “Powerful, Soft Combustion Actuators for Insect-Scale Robots,” was published in the journal *Science* on September 14, 2023. [2, 4] The robot's power source allows it to outperform electric counterparts; its soft combustion actuators can generate forces of 9.5 newtons, compared to about 0.2 newtons for similar robots. [2, 5] This enables it to carry over 22 times its own weight, navigate difficult terrain, and leap approximately 20 times its body length (about 56-60 cm). [2, 3, 5] By varying fuel flow and spark frequency, operators can control the robot's movement, making it crawl, hop, or jump. [2, 3]

This new version integrates advanced reasoning, multimodality, and long-context understanding. Instead of users manually selecting a model, GPT-5 employs a 'smart router' that automatically directs queries to the most appropriate internal model based on the task's complexity, aiming to blend the rapid response times of earlier models with deeper, 'PhD-level' reasoning for more complex problems. Key enhancements include state-of-the-art performance in coding, math, writing, and health, with a significant reduction in factual errors or 'hallucinations'. The model features a large context window of up to 272,000 tokens and natively supports tools like web browsing and image generation within one interface. GPT-5 is being rolled out to all users, including those on the free tier, with different usage limits and access to more powerful versions like GPT-5 Pro for subscribers.
